thread:
erin: Heads-up: we have a regression on multi-GPU throughput after the cudaGraph refactor. Peak tokens/sec down ~18% for 8xA100 tensor-parallel runs. Suspect comm/compute overlap failure — all-reduce looks serialized with matmuls.

mike: ugh. which path? training or serving runtime?

erin: serving runtime path — the capture now uses cudaStreamBeginCapture on the compute stream, then we launch NCCL all-reduces on a separate stream, but profiler shows the all-reduce is blocking the compute stream. timeline: compute kernels wait until NCCL ends rather than overlap.

anya: can you paste the nsys timeline snippet? even a short ascii summary helps. :thinking_face:

erin: pasted below (nsys flame simplified):
```
Time ->
[compute_stream] kernel_A |---KERNEL---|      |---KERNEL---|
                      \                                   /
                       \                                 /
[allreduce_stream]     ---ALLREDUCE----|-----------------|\
```
Basically the compute kernels have gaps where they stall waiting for allreduce to finish. The gaps align with allreduce on other stream.
```
### nvprof slice
GPU id 0:  matmul  120us  start 10.2ms -> end 10.32ms
GPU id 0:  ncclAllReduce  2.1ms  start 10.32ms -> end 12.42ms
GPU id 0:  matmul  115us  start 12.42ms -> end 12.535ms
```
Shows compute waits until nccl completes.

mike: sounds like either capture semantics forced default-stream sync or NCCL enqueues into a stream that introduces device-side dependency. Did the refactor change stream flags?

erin: we switched streams to `cudaStreamDefault` for capture convenience previously, but refactor moved to `cudaStreamBeginCapture(compute_stream, cudaStreamCaptureModeThreadLocal)` then launched NCCL on `allreduce_stream` (created with default flags). I think cudaGraph capture captures host enqueues differently and causes an implicit dependency.

perf-bot: automated check: recent PR 4823 modified graph capture code: replaced cudaStreamCreateWithFlags(cudaStreamNonBlocking) -> cudaStreamDefault in 4 callsites. CI perf test shows 15-20% regression on multi-gpu.

anya: two things to consider: (1) NCCL may create internal synchronization with the captured stream if operations are recorded during capture on another stream; (2) default stream semantics (legacy) can create cross-stream ordering. We should ensure both streams are non-blocking and use explicit stream-aware NCCL calls.

mike: do we use `ncclComm` per-stream or reuse same comm across streams?

erin: we reuse the comm across streams (one comm per rank) and pass the stream to `ncclAllReduce` as usual. code snippet:
```
// simplified
cudaStream_t compute_stream, allreduce_stream;
cudaStreamBeginCapture(compute_stream, cudaStreamCaptureModeThreadLocal);
launch_matmul_kernels(compute_stream);
cudaStreamEndCapture(compute_stream, &graph);
// later
ncclAllReduce(..., allreduce_stream);
cudaGraphLaunch(graph, compute_stream);
```
Order is: capture compute, end capture -> launch allreduce on allreduce_stream -> launch graph on compute_stream. We hoped the NCCL on allreduce_stream would run concurrently, but it seems the graph launch serializes it.

devon: try swapping ordering: launch NCCL first on allreduce_stream, then cudaGraphLaunch on compute_stream. If the graph launch is enqueuing work that depends on host-side events, it might implicitly wait for previous host enqueues. But more robust is to avoid launching graph while other streams have outstanding comms that you expect to overlap.

mike: also check how cudaGraph captures and replay interact with stream synchronization. If the graph contains kernels that use the default stream internally or if the capture turned on thread-local capture, the runtime might insert stream waits.

erin: tried reorder: launching NCCL before graph helped a bit but still not ideal. I instrumented with cudaEventRecord between operations and saw `cudaEventQuery` on compute stream returning not-ready until NCCL finished. So it looks like the graph replay creates a dependency.

anya: alternative: capture the entire sequence including comms into the graph so replay contains the NCCL ops and scheduler handles ordering. But NCCL collective capture into CUDA graphs requires using the stream for NCCL calls during capture and using `ncclLaunch` patterns that are graph-capture friendly. Do we have that option?

erin: we can try, but NCCL operations during capture require using the same stream and calling NCCL ops while in capture. Currently we capture only compute kernels to keep graphs reusable across sequence lengths. Capturing NCCL would entangle graph with batch size and kv-cache behavior.

devon: small patch I prototyped: create both streams with `cudaStreamCreateWithFlags(..., cudaStreamNonBlocking)`, ensure we call `ncclAllReduce(..., allreduce_stream)` during capture window on that stream, then end capture. Another approach: use `cudaGraphInstantiate` and set stream dependency by `cudaGraphAddMemcpyNode`/event nodes to explicitly express overlap.

patch snippet:
```
cudaStreamCreateWithFlags(&compute_stream, cudaStreamNonBlocking);
cudaStreamCreateWithFlags(&allreduce_stream, cudaStreamNonBlocking);
// begin capture on both? capture only compute but enqueue NCCL into allreduce_stream during capture
cudaStreamBeginCapture(compute_stream, cudaStreamCaptureModeGlobal);
// ensure NCCL uses allreduce_stream but we issue it now so it's recorded
ncclAllReduce(..., allreduce_stream);
launch_matmul_kernels(compute_stream);
cudaStreamEndCapture(compute_stream, &graph);
```
This records cross-stream nodes.

mike: be careful: older CUDA/NCCL combos had limited support for capturing collectives. Which driver/runtime/NCCL versions are we on?

erin: infra: driver 535.86, CUDA 12.1, NCCL 2.18. We test on 535.x in CI. perf-bot flagged that the regression surfaced on 535 drivers.

anya: NCCL 2.18 has some graph capture behavior but it's finicky. If it's unreliable, safer short-term fix is to revert graph capture for the stage that overlaps with collectives, or split the pipeline so collectives run in a dedicated non-captured codepath.

erin: agreed. I'll open a small revert PR for the capture around the collective boundary so we don't regress production perf. Also will add an integration test that runs a tiny all-reduce + matmul and asserts overlap (nsys check) to prevent future regressions.

mike: SGTM. For the longer term, let's add a design doc: options are (A) capture compute+comm together (if supported), (B) make collectives part of the graph via NCCL capture-safe calls, (C) avoid graphs across collective boundaries and use manual stream/event orchestration. Each has tradeoffs for reuse, memory, and KV cache semantics.

devon: I'll prototype (A) in a branch and post results. If we can get reliable capture with NCCL on our infra, it might be the cleanest for perf.

perf-bot: perf test queued: perf/ci/graph-nccl/8xA100 will run on the revert branch and the prototype branch. results ETA ~ 3h.

mike: thanks everyone. Erin, can you include the minimal repro (nsys + short harness) in the PR? that'll speed validation.

erin: yes, attaching quick repro pointer: https://git.internal/redwood/infer/repoharness/graph-nccl-repro (private link). will send PR in ~30m. :thumbsup:

mike: perfect. keep us posted. :fire:
